notes.meaning: After seven days of waiting and preparing at the tabernacle, Aaron and his sons were ready to begin their work. Moses called together the leaders of Israel so they could witness the priests take up their official duties. Serving God requires patient preparation before active ministry begins.

Moses instructed Aaron to bring a young bull and a ram with no physical defects for his own offering. Many ancient writers note that offering a calf reminded Aaron of his past sin with the golden calf. Even after a week of special ceremonies, Aaron was still a sinner who needed God's mercy first.

Aaron was told to direct the people of Israel to bring their own animals for sacrifice. Now that Aaron was high priest, he took over the role of teaching the people how to approach God. Every animal had to be healthy and without defect, showing that God deserves our best.

Moses added peace offerings and a grain offering so the people could celebrate friendly fellowship with God. He gave them the wonderful promise that the Lord Himself would appear to them that very day. When God's people obey His directions, He promises to draw near to them.

The people brought all the animals and grain to the entrance of the sacred tent, exactly as Moses directed. The entire gathering stood together with quiet respect before the Lord. True worship starts when God's people listen and obey His word together.

Moses explained that carrying out these commands was the path to seeing the glory of the Lord. God's glory means the dazzling brightness and heavy weight of His holy presence. God often reveals His presence when His people walk in careful obedience.

Moses told Aaron to step up to the altar to make atonement, which means removing sin so people can be at peace with God. Aaron had to make atonement for his own sins before he could do anything for the nation. This showed that human priests are flawed, pointing ahead to Jesus who was sinless and never needed an offering for Himself.

Aaron went to the altar and slaughtered the calf for his own sin offering. By doing this in front of everyone, he openly admitted that he was a sinner who needed forgiveness. Good leaders stay humble and recognize their own need for God's grace.

Aaron's sons caught the blood in a basin and brought it to him at the altar. Aaron dipped his finger into it, smeared the blood on the four raised corners of the bronze altar, and poured the rest at its base. This showed that blood was needed to cleanse the altar where God met His people.

Aaron burned the internal fat and organs on the altar because the richest portions belonged to God. The meat and hide were carried outside the camp and completely destroyed by fire. Because this offering was for the priest himself, he could not eat any of it, showing he could not carry away his own guilt.

Aaron then slaughtered the ram for his burnt offering, which symbolized total surrender to God. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against all sides of the altar. This showed that complete devotion to God can only happen after sin has been taken care of.

The sons of Aaron brought the pieces of the animal to him one by one, and he placed them on the altar fire. Aaron washed the inner parts and legs with clean water before burning them with the rest of the ram. Worship must be handled with care and reverent order, reflecting God's desire for pure hearts.

After offering for himself, Aaron took the male goat meant for the sins of the people. He slaughtered it and presented it just like his own sin offering. Only after a minister has been forgiven and cleansed by God can he truly serve the needs of others.

Aaron brought the people's burnt offering and offered it according to the exact rules God had given earlier. He did not invent new rituals or rush through the steps. God is honored when we worship Him according to His instructions rather than our own ideas.

Aaron brought the grain offering, scooped up a handful of flour mixed with oil, and burned it on the altar. This gift was added right alongside the regular morning lamb that was offered every day. Special moments of worship should never cause us to neglect our daily habits of prayer.

Aaron slaughtered the ox and ram as a peace offering for the community, and his sons brought him the blood to splash on the altar. The peace offering celebrated a restored, friendly relationship between God and His people. It reminded the nation that God welcomes forgiven sinners into peaceful communion with Himself.

The priests gathered the choice fat portions from the animals and burned them on the altar as a pleasing gift to God. Aaron then waved the breast and right thigh back and forth before the Lord to set them apart as food for the priests. This shared meal showed that God, the priest, and the worshiper were now enjoying peace together.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest the mention of waving the right thigh was copied from Leviticus 7, because elsewhere the right thigh is usually lifted up as a contribution rather than waved.

notes.meaning: Aaron finished the sacrifices, raised his hands toward the gathered crowd, and spoke a blessing over them. Blessings from God follow directly from the blood of sacrifice that takes away sin. Aaron's gesture pointed forward to Jesus, who lifted His hands to bless His disciples before returning to heaven.

Moses led Aaron inside the sacred tent to show him how to serve in the Holy Place, and they prayed for God's blessing. When they came back out and blessed the people together, the radiant brightness of the Lord's glory appeared to everyone. God gladly reveals His presence to those who seek Him in united prayer.

Supernatural fire flashed out from the presence of the Lord and instantly consumed the offerings on the altar. This miracle proved that God fully accepted the new priesthood and their sacrifices. Overcome with awe and relief, the people shouted with joy and bowed low with their faces to the ground.
